As of this pass SEG publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable API surface; this profile is maintained as a company/identity record rather than an API provider.

providers.name: Deutscher Wetterdienst
providers.description: Deutscher Wetterdienst (DWD) is Germany's national meteorological service, a federal agency under the Ministry for Digital and Transport, responsible for weather and climate services, warnings, and the national climate archive. Its geospatial surface is an OGC-standard GeoServer at maps.dwd.de serving forecast, radar, warning and climate layers to any WMS or WFS client without a key.

providers.name: Eurac Research
providers.description: Eurac Research is a private research centre in Bolzano, Italy, working across alpine environment, earth observation, health and autonomy studies. Its MAPS portal publishes research datasets — snow cover, land use, climate and remote-sensing products for the Alpine region — through an OGC-standard GeoServer callable anonymously by any GIS client.

providers.name: Flanders Marine Institute
providers.description: The Flanders Marine Institute (Vlaams Instituut voor de Zee, VLIZ) is the Belgian coordination and information platform for marine research, and the operator of Marine Regions, the World Register of Marine Species gazetteer infrastructure and the EMODnet data portals. Its geospatial estate is one of the largest openly callable marine OGC surfaces in Europe.

providers.name: Spacebel s.a.
providers.description: Spacebel s.a. is a Belgian software company building flight and ground software for space missions, including on-board software for ESA missions and Earth-observation ground segments, catalogues and data-access services. Its GIS estate serves Sentinel-derived Earth-observation products through OGC-standard web services.

providers.name: 51Talk
providers.description: 51Talk is an online English-language education platform that connects learners with certified teachers through one-on-one live video lessons. Founded in 2011 and listed on the NYSE, the company operates across 90+ countries with a large base of accredited teachers, delivering a structured curriculum and ready-made teaching materials for both children and adult learners. Following a strategic shift, 51Talk focuses on international markets outside mainland China, including the Philippines and the broader Southeast Asia region, and recruits teachers globally. It is a consumer education company backed by DCM Ventures; as of this profile it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface, so this repo carries only identity and domain-security signals.

providers.name: AssetWorks
providers.description: AssetWorks is an enterprise fleet and asset management software company with more than 40 years of history and over 1,000 customers across commercial and private fleets, government and public works, and higher education. Its products include FleetFocus fleet and enterprise asset management (EAM), Active Assets fixed-asset tracking, Recoup Ops surplus management, and Scan and Validate mobile inventory management. AssetWorks sells on-premise and hosted enterprise software to large fleet and facility operators; as of this profile it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or self-serve API program. This repo is a company profile in the API Evangelist network, backed by Battery Ventures.

providers.name: Playbook
providers.description: Playbook is a career-growth platform for women that combines expert-led Masterclasses with an engaged professional community, enabling members to keep learning, build skills, and advance into leadership roles. Its tagline "Connect, Learn, Invest" reflects a focus on peer connection, ongoing education, and investing in one's own career. Playbook is backed by 500 Global and Bain Capital Ventures. As of this profile the company operates a consumer marketing and community web experience and does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer documentation.

providers.name: UberSense
providers.description: UberSense was a Boston, Massachusetts sports-technology startup whose mobile app provided slow-motion video capture and analysis for coaching athletes, from recreational to Olympic and professional levels. Backed by GV (Google Ventures), UberSense was acquired by Hudl in September 2014 and its technology folded into Hudl's sports video analysis products. The ubersense.com website is now defunct (a decommissioned Heroku app) and the company publishes no public API surface.

providers.name: Englease Technologies SPV Ltd
providers.description: Englease is an online English language learning platform serving students across the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region, founded by Omar Shihan and headquartered in Dubai Internet City, UAE. The platform blends live classes running 16 hours a day across all seven days, self-paced on-demand courses, pronunciation and practice tools, and conversation clubs, with proficiency-based learning paths from beginner to advanced and UK-accredited certifications. Englease serves individuals, corporations, schools, and specific industries including hospitality, call centers, retail, banking, and healthcare. Englease Technologies SPV Ltd is a portfolio company of 500 Global, added to the API Evangelist network for tracking. The consumer product is delivered through a web/app experience; no public developer API surface has been identified.

providers.name: Springboard
providers.description: Springboard is an online education company offering mentor-led, career-focused bootcamps and courses in software engineering, data science, data analytics, UX/UI design, cybersecurity, and machine learning. Programs pair a structured, self-paced curriculum with 1:1 industry mentorship, career coaching, and a job guarantee on eligible tracks. Springboard was surfaced from a 500 Global portfolio list and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; it operates as a consumer/B2B learning platform and does not currently publish a public developer API, so this profile carries identity and security-posture signals rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Barnes & Noble Education
providers.description: Barnes & Noble Education, Inc. (NYSE: BNED) is one of the largest operators of college bookstores in the United States, operating physical and virtual campus stores alongside digital course-materials and educational services. BNED reaches more than 5.7 million students through 1,125+ physical and virtual stores across higher education and K-12 institutions, primarily through its Barnes & Noble College Booksellers subsidiary and the MBS Textbook Exchange wholesale business. Flagship offerings include the First Day and First Day Complete affordable-access course-materials programs, BNC OER+ digital courseware, faculty adoption tools, campus retail and ecommerce services, and BNC AI Tools. BNED separated from Barnes & Noble, Inc. in August 2015 and is not affiliated with the Barnes & Noble retail bookstore chain. This repository captures any APIs, developer tools, and machine-readable artifacts associated with BNED. No public developer APIs or developer portal have been identified at this time; integrations with campus systems and learning-management systems are delivered through institutional partnerships rather than a public API surface.

providers.name: Lego
providers.description: The LEGO Group is a Danish toy company and the world's largest manufacturer of interlocking plastic building bricks. The company extends its brand across video games, theme parks, movies, educational products, and licensed sets for children and adults. LEGO does not currently publish a public developer API or developer portal; consumer-facing systems and partner integrations are closed. A public GitHub organization hosts internal engineering tooling and open-source contributions.

providers.name: 9Slides
providers.description: 9Slides was a cloud-based presentation platform, founded by Ruchit Garg in 2011, that let users combine slide decks (PowerPoint, PDF, Keynote, Prezi, Excel) with synchronized video and deliver them through an HTML5 player viewable on desktop, tablet, and mobile. It operated on a freemium model, charging for premium features such as an ad-free player, password-protected presentations, and viewer analytics, and later pivoted toward learning and training. Backed by 500 Global, the company was acquired by employee-engagement platform Limeade. The 9slides.com domain no longer serves the product and now resolves to a parked/redirect landing page; no public API, developer portal, SDK, or documentation is currently published.

providers.name: Cultivate
providers.description: Cultivate was an AI-powered digital leadership and coaching platform that analyzed leaders' own opt-in digital communication data to deliver hyper-personalized, privacy-preserving coaching insights and recommendations for people managers. Founded through an Entrepreneur in Residence program at Samsung NEXT by Joseph Freed, Samir Meghani, and Andy Horng, and backed by Trinity Ventures, Silicon Valley Data Capital, and Bloomberg Beta, Cultivate was acquired by employee listening and people-analytics company Perceptyx on February 15, 2022, where it became the basis for Perceptyx's "Cultivate Intelligent Coaching" product. Cultivate operated as an enterprise HR/leadership SaaS and did not publish a public developer API or OpenAPI. This profile is retained as a portfolio-lead record; the company no longer exists as an independent entity.

providers.name: Luna Park
providers.description: Luna Park is a consumer-sector company surfaced as a portfolio company of GV (Google Ventures) and added to the API Evangelist network. Its registered domain lunapark.com now redirects (HTTP 301) to meetquinn.ai — Quinn, described on-site as an AI training platform focused on "operational readiness for the trades." As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a minimal marketing landing page with no public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI specification, or other machine-readable API surface. Domain-security posture was probed live: TLS 1.3 with SPF and DMARC (quarantine) present; no HSTS, DNSSEC, or CAA records.

providers.name: Mitro *
providers.description: Mitro was a password manager for individuals and teams, founded in 2012 in New York City by Vijay Pandurangan, Evan Jones, and Adam Hilss (former Google/Serious Eats engineers). It let multiple people securely share and control logins to a single account, architected around cloud storage with password databases encrypted client-side using keys derived from the user master password. Mitro raised $1.2M in seed funding from Google Ventures (GV) and Matrix Partners. On July 31, 2014 the team joined Twitter and released the Mitro source code on GitHub as free software under the GPL. The hosted Mitro service shut down on October 6, 2015; its open-source successor is Passopolis. The company is defunct and publishes no live API, developer portal, or reachable domain today.

providers.name: Naranga
providers.description: Naranga is a cloud-based franchise management platform for franchisors and multi-location brands, covering franchise sales CRM and lead management (emaximation), operations and multi-location support (nCompass), employee and franchisee training (nSpire), field audits and inspections, task and job scheduling, and local/multi-channel marketing. API access model: Naranga does NOT publish a documented public or self-serve developer API. There is no developer portal, no published API reference, no OpenAPI/Swagger definition, no SDKs, and no self-serve API keys as of this entry. Integrations with third-party systems (for example Twilio, RingCentral, Microsoft 365, AssureSign, and lead-capture/Zapier-style connectors) exist but are delivered through Naranga's partner and professional-services onboarding (typically a multi-week implementation scoped per brand), not through open, documented, developer-facing endpoints. Pricing is quote-based / contact-sales.

providers.name: Polyup
providers.description: Let'sMOD (formerly Polyup) is a Sunnyvale, California company founded in 2015 that builds a consumer platform where users aged 8 and up can play, modify, remix, and share short 3D microgames and AI-powered interactive memes. Originally a computational-thinking and math learning tool under the Polyup brand, the product has evolved into a generative-AI-driven microgame and viral-content community at letsmod.com. Let'sMOD is a 500 Global portfolio company. It exposes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal today; its public GitHub organization contains only internal CLI tooling and configuration. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead and enriched via live domain-security probing.

providers.name: VR Motion
providers.description: VR Motion Corp develops virtual-reality driver-training simulation systems, marketed under its RealDrive product, delivering true-to-life driving simulations that the company says achieve over 70% greater skills retention than traditional training. It serves commercial fleets, last-mile delivery operations, first responders, and driving schools. VR Motion is a 500 Global portfolio company. As of the 2026-07-21 enrichment pass its public web presence is a marketing site with no developer API, docs, SDK, or developer portal, so there is no machine-readable API surface to catalog.

providers.name: YOURIKA
providers.description: YOURIKA (YOURIKA Labs) is a Kitchener-Waterloo, Canada AI platform and venture studio that creates and scales purpose-built, verticalized AI ventures in partnership with industry experts, prioritizing accuracy, trust, and measurable outcomes over technology-first approaches. Its ventures include smart'n, a nurse-first intelligence and learning platform that helps nurses learn, grow, and make more informed decisions throughout their careers, and Retain / Workforce Intelligence for senior and long-term care, which helps operators identify, hire, and retain caregivers while reducing turnover. yourikaLABS also offers AI advisory services connecting businesses with experts to build data-driven strategies and roadmaps. YOURIKA is backed by Amazon, Techstars (Amazon Alexa Accelerator), and the University of Waterloo. The company exposes no bespoke public developer API; its marketing site is built on Wix and advertises a Wix Site MCP endpoint plus an llms.txt for agentic access.

providers.name: Respondus
providers.description: Respondus builds assessment-integrity tools for online exams - most notably LockDown Browser, a custom browser that locks down the testing environment, and Respondus Monitor, an automated webcam-based online proctoring service that adds AI-assisted review on top of LockDown Browser. Over 2,000 institutions across 50+ countries use Respondus to deliver hundreds of millions of online exams a year. Respondus does not publish a self-service public developer API. Its products reach learning platforms through LMS integration rather than an open REST surface - native plugins/building blocks plus the IMS Global LTI (Learning Tools Interoperability) standard for Blackboard, Brightspace, Canvas, Moodle, Sakai, and Schoology, and a privately-licensed LockDown Browser SDK for third-party assessment platforms that must be arranged through Respondus sales. No public OpenAPI, developer keys, or documented endpoints are offered.

providers.name: GetSetup
providers.description: GetSetUp is a consumer education platform delivering live, interactive online classes designed specifically for older adults. Learners join expert-led sessions to build digital skills, stay physically and mentally active, pursue hobbies, and connect with a global community of peers. The catalog spans technology how-tos, health and wellness, finance, creativity, and social classes, offered in multiple languages across regions. GetSetUp partners with health plans, employers, libraries, and government programs to make classes accessible. Backed by Cowboy Ventures, it operates a business-to-consumer learning experience rather than a public developer API; this profile tracks its public web surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: GoGuardian
providers.description: GoGuardian is a K-12 education technology company whose suite - Admin (DNS and device content filtering for CIPA compliance), Teacher (classroom management and student engagement), and Beacon (student safety and self-harm / suicide risk detection) - is administered through web dashboards rather than a broadly published public API. GoGuardian's integration model is primarily roster ingestion - it syncs organizations, students, teachers, guardians, and classes from district Student Information Systems via the IMS Global / 1EdTech OneRoster 1.1 REST API (using a Consumer ID / Secret and a OneRoster URL), Clever, ClassLink, and Google Classroom, and it consumes Google Workspace admin APIs on the district's behalf. A developer / partner documentation portal exists at based.goguardian.com ("GoGuardian Based Docs"), but GoGuardian's own outbound developer API surface is partner-gated and not openly published. The API entries below are honestly modeled logical surfaces, not a confirmed public REST catalog.

providers.name: SVAcademy
providers.description: SV Academy is a tech-sales training and talent-placement organization that runs an intensive Sales Development Representative (SDR) program and places pre-trained, job-ready graduates with employers at no placement fee. It has trained more than 6,000 graduates across the U.S. and Canada and is a portfolio company of 500 Global. SV Academy serves two audiences — job seekers who complete the SDR training program with no prior experience or degree required, and employers who hire and onboard vetted, pre-trained SDR talent. The organization publishes no public developer API surface at this time; this profile was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline from SV Academy's public web presence.

providers.name: 83 Sciences
providers.description: 83 Sciences is an AI-native materials-discovery company (Y Combinator Summer 2026) that helps research labs unlock value from unpublished and discarded experimental data. Roughly 90% of experimental data never reaches publication; 83 Sciences works on-site with researchers to capture and structure that hidden data into a queryable database, then applies AI-powered analysis and generative models to learn from a lab's full experimental history — including failed experiments — to surface novel materials, co-authored manuscripts, and patents. Founded by researchers from MIT, Stanford, Harvard, and Columbia and based in San Francisco. The company currently ships no public API or developer surface; this profile tracks its identity for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Epic! Creations
providers.description: Epic! Creations, Inc. operates Epic, an award-winning digital reading and learning platform for children twelve and under. The service gives families and educators unlimited access to a library of more than 40,000 books, audiobooks, and learning videos, with reading-level personalization, quizzes, and progress tracking. Epic offers a consumer family subscription and Epic School, a version that is free for teachers and students during the school day via class codes. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network. Epic is a business-to-consumer application and does not publish a public developer program, API, or SDK surface.

providers.name: Mentor Spaces
providers.description: Mentor Spaces is a structured mentorship platform that helps nonprofits, universities, and companies launch, manage, and measure mentorship programs at scale. The software handles automated mentor-mentee matching, scheduling, communication, and real-time outcome tracking so organizations can secure and renew grant funding with funder-ready impact reports, improve student persistence and career outcomes, engage alumni in time-bound structured mentorship, and run skills-based volunteering and corporate CSR/ESG programs. A public developer API and custom integrations are offered only on the enterprise Thrive tier (with SSO); no public API documentation is published. Founded by Chris Motley and backed by Techstars.

providers.name: TaskHuman
providers.description: TaskHuman was a mobile-first, on-demand human coaching platform that connected employees with live 1:1 video coaching across wellbeing, fitness, leadership, professional growth, sales and mentorship topics, sold to employers as a benefit and delivered through iOS, Android and web apps plus Slack and Microsoft Teams integrations. The San Francisco Bay Area company raised roughly $35M from investors including U.S. Venture Partners and Madrona and marketed a coach network spanning more than a thousand skill areas. The company ceased operations in 2026; as of this profile the entire taskhuman.com origin answers HTTP 401 behind an nginx HTTP Basic authentication wall and the product's API and application hosts no longer resolve, so no developer program, documentation or machine-readable contract remains reachable.

providers.name: Duane Morris
providers.description: Duane Morris LLP is a Philadelphia-headquartered, full-service U.S. and international law firm founded in 1904 by Russell Duane, Steven Heckscher, and Roland S. Morris. Chaired by Matthew A. Taylor, the firm describes itself as "a law firm with more than 900 attorneys in offices across the United States and internationally" — with a U.S. footprint spanning the East Coast, Texas, the Mountain West, and California, plus international offices in London, Singapore, Vietnam (Hanoi, Ho Chi Minh City), Shanghai, Myanmar, and joint ventures/alliances reaching Mexico and Latin America. An Am Law 100 firm since 2001, Duane Morris is known for depth in intellectual property (including patent prosecution and PTAB practice), trial and appellate litigation, real estate, corporate transactions, employment, healthcare, cannabis, and life sciences. The firm publishes an extensive LexBlog-powered thought-leadership network of more than 50 practice-area blogs, all of which expose RSS 2.0 feeds via the standard WordPress /feed/ convention. Duane Morris does not expose any public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI spec, GraphQL endpoint, webhooks, status page, or developer portal; the GitHub organization github.com/duanemorris exists but has no public repositories. The firm's only machine-readable surfaces are the RSS feeds of its blog network.

providers.name: Givecampus
providers.description: GiveCampus is a digital-first fundraising and alumni-engagement platform built for educational institutions - K-12 schools, colleges, universities, and their affiliated foundations, alumni associations, and nonprofits. The platform provides online giving pages, Giving Days, crowdfunding and peer-to-peer (advocacy) fundraising, matching and challenge gifts, event and volunteer management, donor management and advancement CRM tooling, payment processing, and stewardship and engagement features that help advancement teams raise more money at a lower cost. Founded in 2015 and backed by Y Combinator, GiveCampus is used by thousands of schools and institutions across the United States and internationally. This API Evangelist profile tracks GiveCampus as a company in the network; the company operates a closed SaaS product and does not publish a public developer API, so this record is identity- and infrastructure-focused.

providers.name: Jewelbots
providers.description: Jewelbots makes smart, codable friendship bracelets designed to teach kids (primarily tween girls) to code. The wearable is an Arduino-compatible, Bluetooth Low Energy device built on a Nordic nRF chipset that friends can program with an Arduino IDE library and firmware, with a companion iOS/Android app for pairing and messaging. The project is largely open source: the Jewelbots GitHub organization publishes the Arduino library, firmware, companion app, and hardware/toolchain repositories. Jewelbots was a 500 Global (500 Startups) portfolio company; jewelbots.com now runs as a Shopify storefront. It is a hardware/firmware and education company rather than a web API provider, and exposes no first-party public HTTP/OpenAPI API.

providers.name: igetget
providers.description: igetget is the English name for 得到 (Dedao), a Chinese knowledge-service and lifelong-learning platform operated by Beijing Siwei Zaowu Information Technology Co., Ltd. (北京思维造物信息科技股份有限公司), the company behind Luojisiwei (罗辑思维) founded by Luo Zhenyu. The app sells curated courses, expert lectures, ebooks, and audiobooks across finance, economics, law, management, psychology, and self-improvement, alongside an enterprise edition, a web edition, and the annual "Time's Friend" (时间的朋友) New Year's Eve lecture. It is a consumer content product; enrichment found no public API specification or developer documentation, only an open-platform (开放平台) login surface at open.igetget.com. Backed by Qiming Venture Partners.

providers.name: Knowmia.com
providers.description: Knowmia was an education-focused video platform used by instructors to create, share, and assign instructional video and lessons. The brand was operated by TechSmith alongside Camtasia and Snagit, and was marketed as Knowmia and Knowmia Pro for classroom and campus video. TechSmith retired Knowmia Pro in early 2025 and now directs former Knowmia customers to TechSmith Screencast, which offers comparable asynchronous video sharing, commenting, and review and integrates with Snagit and Camtasia. As of July 2026 knowmia.com issues an HTTP 301 redirect to the TechSmith Screencast product page. Knowmia publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, CLI, or machine-readable specifications; this profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a retired/absorbed entry for historical and lineage purposes.

providers.name: Microverse
providers.description: Microverse is an online education platform that trains people worldwide to become remote software developers, founded by Ariel Camus with the stated mission of connecting one million people to remote jobs by 2030. Its model pairs students across time zones for peer collaboration that mirrors distributed engineering teams, and it historically charged tuition only after graduates secured a job. Microverse also runs Leap, an English-practice platform for developers. It is a private, distributed company backed by investors including Y Combinator, Hack.VC, and General Catalyst. Microverse does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation; this profile captures its public web presence and security posture.

providers.name: Drexel University
providers.description: Drexel University is a private research university in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, with roughly 24,000 students and a Carnegie R1 (very high research activity) classification. Drexel is internationally known for its cooperative education (co-op) program, which embeds full-time professional work experience into undergraduate degrees. Core enterprise systems run on Ellucian Banner, surfaced to students and staff through the DrexelOne portal. Drexel does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or open data portal; the organization's GitHub org (drexel-university) currently lists no public repositories, and library, catalog, and IT service pages do not expose documented integration endpoints. This profile is maintained as a tier-3 no-public-API index entry.

providers.name: eSpark
providers.description: eSpark is a K-5 adaptive learning platform that extends a district's core reading and math programs with differentiated, standards-aligned practice in reading, math, and writing. The platform uses adaptive lesson sequencing that adjusts difficulty to each student's performance, interest-based content, and real-time feedback to deliver personalized instruction, and it reports back to teachers and administrators on student progress. eSpark serves 10,000+ schools and districts nationwide and rosters students through Clever, ClassLink, Google Classroom, and QR-code sign-in. eSpark was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network; it publishes no public developer API, so this profile captures company identity, its public web properties, and probed domain-security posture rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Wikifarmer
providers.description: Wikifarmer is a global agricultural platform that connects producers with buyers through a B2B marketplace for agricultural products and educates farmers through expert-reviewed content. It provides practical agricultural knowledge, market access, and price insights for farmers, agribusinesses, traders, and food companies worldwide, with a multilingual educational library covering crop cultivation, livestock, sustainability, soil management, irrigation, pest control, and post-harvest handling, alongside a global marketplace connecting suppliers and buyers and a price-insights service for agricultural commodities.

providers.name: Ilumno
providers.description: Ilumno is a Latin American education technology company that helps higher education institutions grow and modernize through digital transformation. Its services span student acquisition and retention (Growth), online and virtual learning platforms (Virtuality), and real-time analytics and student-data management tools, all delivered on its Growth Engine technology platform. Ilumno reports supporting more than 220,000 students across the region, with offices in Bogota (Colombia), Dallas (USA) and Amsterdam (Netherlands). The company is backed by Insight Partners.

providers.name: Examity
providers.description: Examity is an online exam proctoring and test integrity platform used by universities, certification bodies, and enterprises to authenticate test-takers and monitor online assessments. It offers automated (AI/ML) proctoring, live proctoring, audit-based review, and ID verification, and integrates with learning management systems (Canvas, Blackboard, D2L Brightspace, Moodle, Sakai, Schoology, and others). Examity's programmatic surface is a partner/LMS integration - single sign-on via IMS LTI (consumer key plus shared secret) and a partner integration REST API that platform vendors use to register exams, schedule proctoring appointments, launch sessions, and retrieve completion status and integrity flags. Access is gated - there is no public self-service developer portal, and integration keys plus the integration manual are provided on request via developers@examity.com. Because no endpoints are publicly documented, the APIs below are modeled from the known integration model rather than a published reference.

providers.name: Atomica Informatics
providers.description: Atomica Informatics is an independent health-informatics consultancy founded and run by Dr Heather Leslie, specialising in what it calls "little data" design: the modelling of atomic clinical data so that individual data points carry consistent format and reliable meaning across projects, domains and systems instead of being locked into single-purpose silos. The practice delivers openEHR archetype and template authoring, clinical knowledge governance, clinician engagement, and openEHR clinical-modelling training - a two-day introductory course, advanced modelling workshops, and ongoing remote mentoring for in-house modelling teams. Dr Leslie pioneered the openEHR clinical modelling methodology in volunteer roles at the openEHR Foundation from 2006 and co-leads its Clinical Program. Atomica Informatics operates no API of its own; the machine-readable standards its work depends on are published by the openEHR Foundation.

providers.name: Marker Learning
providers.description: Marker Learning is a special-education technology company that provides AI-powered report-writing tools for school districts and evaluation teams. Its platform ingests referral and assessment documents and automatically drafts comprehensive psychological and educational evaluation reports, citing its sources for transparency, supporting multiple assessment and rating scales, and running built-in compliance checks. The company emphasizes FERPA and NIST CSF compliance. Marker Learning was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass it publishes no public API, developer portal, or API documentation.

providers.name: Elwyn
providers.description: Elwyn is a Pennsylvania-headquartered nonprofit human services organization founded in 1852, providing services to children and adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities, autism, and behavioral health needs. Elwyn describes itself as "the longest-running human services nonprofit of its kind in the nation," operating across Pennsylvania, Delaware, New Jersey, and California with approximately 4,000 employees. The organization delivers six core service lines: Adult Behavioral Health Services, Children's Behavioral Health Services, Crisis Services, Early Learning Services, Educational Services, and Intellectual and Developmental Disabilities Services. Elwyn is a service-delivery nonprofit, not a software or API provider. It publishes no public APIs, OpenAPI documents, SDKs, developer portal, or open-data feeds. Its digital presence is limited to its marketing site (elwyn.org), program pages, news, and donation/contact forms. This profile documents the organization's mission and the absence of any public API or developer surface.

providers.name: Kyros College Prep
providers.description: Kyros (kyros.ai) is an AI-driven college preparation and admissions platform. In the company's own words, it is "a College Prep Platform by former Googlers, Admissions Officers, and Professors" that "uses AI to offer 100K+ summer and financial aid programs." The product combines student assessments for college and major fit, one-on-one counseling, college essay and letter-of-recommendation support, extracurricular and summer-program discovery, and structured program tracks such as Future You Lab, the UC Bootcamp, and industry immersion and research programs. Kyros also sells through partner channels, with education-partner, VAR, counselor-advisory, college-success, and Fortune 1000 employer offerings, and publishes a large admissions blog. As of 2026-07-19 Kyros publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API description.

providers.name: Virtual Internship Partners
providers.description: Virtual Internships (Virtual Internship Partners) is a global EdTech platform that connects learners, universities, and host companies to deliver guaranteed remote internships across career fields including finance, legal, healthcare, media and communications, supply chain, hospitality, real estate, HR, and sustainability. Backed by 500 Global, it pairs students and graduates with mentored, project-based work experience at companies worldwide. Added to the API Evangelist network from a VC portfolio and enriched by the pipeline; the company publishes a marketing website and a Rank Math llms.txt but exposes no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Knowable
providers.description: Knowable was a mobile audio-learning company that united world-class experts, thinkers, and storytellers to produce structured audio courses for curious minds — an "audio courses" take on online learning delivered as serialized lessons rather than one-off podcasts. Founded by the Bit Kitchen team and backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z led its round in May 2019), Knowable published expert-led course series across business, creativity, and personal development. The company is no longer operational: knowable.fyi now serves a tombstone notice stating that Knowable has been acquired by Medium and directing former listeners to Medium.com. Knowable never published a public developer program, API, SDKs, or developer documentation, and its GitHub organization (bitkitchen) exposes no public repositories. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical company record from the a16z portfolio; there is no live API surface to catalog.

providers.name: uNow (UniversityNow)
providers.description: UniversityNow, Inc. (uNow) was a San Francisco-based higher-education startup founded in 2011 and backed by 500 Startups (500 Global) that built competency-based, self-paced online degree programs for working adults. It operated New Charter University, acquired Patten University in 2012, and its learning platform was sold to Penn Foster Education Group in 2016 and National University System in 2018. The company is defunct and unow.com now redirects to a dead page; it published no public API.

providers.name: BeConfident
providers.description: BeConfident (Beconfident Inteligencia Artificial em Idiomas Ltda.) is an AI-powered English language-learning platform that lets learners practice through real-time conversations with AI tutors via text, voice, and video, plus guided 24/7 lessons, grammar and pronunciation feedback, and study plans tailored to proficiency level, with access across web, WhatsApp, and smartwatch. It is a consumer EdTech application backed by Prosus Ventures and operating primarily in the Brazilian (Portuguese) market. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface, so this profile is identity-only.

providers.name: Crossfit
providers.description: CrossFit is a fitness brand and training methodology built around constantly varied, high-intensity functional movements that combine strength, conditioning, gymnastics, and weightlifting. The organization operates a global network of independently owned affiliate gyms, delivers a coaching certification and education program (the Level 1 through Level 4 courses and specialty seminars), and produces the annual CrossFit Games competition season. CrossFit was surfaced as a portfolio company of General Catalyst and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead; as of this enrichment pass the company publishes a consumer and affiliate web presence (gym finder, courses, store, Games results) but no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API definition.

providers.name: Anki
providers.description: Anki, Inc. was a consumer robotics and artificial-intelligence company based in San Francisco, founded in 2010 and backed by Andreessen Horowitz, Index Ventures, and J.P. Morgan. It was known for the Cozmo and Vector companion robots and the Anki Drive / Overdrive robotic racing system, which combined computer vision, on-device AI, and mapping/navigation. Anki debuted at Apple's WWDC in 2013, shipped Cozmo in 2016 and Vector in 2018, and published first-party Python and C# SDKs so developers could program the robots over a local connection. Anki ceased operations in May 2019 and its assets were later acquired by Digital Dream Labs. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; the robot SDKs remain the company's public developer surface.

providers.name: Blubblub
providers.description: Blub Blub Inc. is the company behind Speech Blubs, a speech-therapy and language-development app for children aged 1 to 8. Created by speech-language pathologists and child-development experts, the app uses video modeling, speech exercises, face filters, and play-based activities to help kids with speech delays, autism, Down syndrome, and apraxia learn to talk. Speech Blubs is available on iOS and Android, supports English, Spanish, and German, and has been downloaded by over 10 million families worldwide. Blub Blub is a portfolio company of Speedinvest. This is a consumer mobile-app company; it does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal, so the entry is limited to verified company identity and published web properties.

providers.name: Picasso
providers.description: Picasso is an image downloading and caching library for Android, focused on simplicity and minimal disk space usage. It is an open-source project by Square. Picasso is a client-side library, not a hosted HTTP API.

providers.name: 51Talk Koala (koalareading.com)
providers.description: koalareading.com serves 51Talk考拉外教官网, the marketing landing page for 51Talk's "Koala" online English foreign-teacher tutoring product aimed at Chinese K-12 learners. The site is a single-page property (hero banner plus footer) operated by 大生在线（深圳）文化传媒科技有限公司 of Shenzhen under ICP filing 粤ICP备2023085692号, with lizhen01@51talk.com published as the technical support contact. The profile entered the API Evangelist network as a Qiming Venture Partners portfolio lead under the name "koalareading" (考拉阅读 / Koala Reading, a Chinese K-12 reading-comprehension edtech); the domain as observed on 2026-07-19 serves the 51Talk Koala product instead, and the relationship between the two is not asserted here. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, developer portal, documentation, SDK, CLI, or machine-readable discovery surface, so this profile carries only probed evidence.

providers.name: Caraway Health *
providers.description: Caraway Health is a digital health company that provides virtual mental and physical healthcare designed for college and university students, delivered through a mobile app with support offered around the clock. The company partners with higher-education institutions and is backed by GV (Google Ventures). It operates as a direct-to-consumer / campus telehealth provider rather than an API platform; at the time of this enrichment pass no public developer program, API reference, or machine-readable specification was found on its public web surface. Sector: life-sciences / digital health.

providers.name: Collegevine
providers.description: CollegeVine is a Cambridge, Massachusetts company, backed by Menlo Ventures, that has repositioned itself as "the AI operating system for universities." Its platform pairs automated ingestion of data from campus systems (a Data layer) with a unified Ontology of institutional operations and an AI Operations layer of agents, applications, and ML models that connect directly to a university's CRM and admissions workflows. CollegeVine also operates a large consumer-facing college-admissions guidance property (chancing engine, essay guidance, and an AI counselor) at collegevine.com and blog.collegevine.com. As of this profile the company exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, developer portal, or published SDK for its product; engagement is enterprise sales and demo driven. It does maintain an active public GitHub organization of open-source PureScript, Haskell, and TypeScript libraries.

providers.name: Ginger
providers.description: Ginger (formerly Ginger.io) was a behavioral and emotional health company offering on-demand mental health support — coaching, therapy, and psychiatry — delivered through a mobile app and an employer/health-plan benefits model. Surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a Techstars portfolio lead, Ginger merged with Headspace in 2021 to form Headspace Health; the ginger.com domain now redirects to Headspace for Organizations (organizations.headspace.com). Enrichment probing on 2026-07-19 found no independent public API, developer portal, OpenAPI, SDKs, or /.well-known discovery surface — every /.well-known path resolves to a soft-404 Headspace marketing page. This profile is retained as an acquired-company record; the only genuine machine-derivable artifact is the live domain-security posture of ginger.com.

providers.name: Graham Holdings
providers.description: Graham Holdings (NYSE: GHC) is a diversified holding company with operations in education, television broadcasting, digital media, manufacturing, healthcare, automotive, restaurants, and custom framing. Principal subsidiaries include Kaplan (educational services), Graham Media Group and Social News Desk (broadcasting and social media tools), The Slate Group and Foreign Policy (digital publishing), Code3 and City Cast (digital marketing and local news), Hoover Treated Wood Products, Joyce/Dayton, Group Dekko, and Forney (manufacturing), Graham Healthcare Group (home health and hospice), Graham Automotive (dealerships), Clyde's Restaurant Group (including Old Ebbitt Grill), and Framebridge (online custom framing). No public developer APIs have been identified across the portfolio.

providers.name: Leaders In Tech
providers.description: Leaders In Tech (LIT) is a leadership accelerator for startup founders and technology executives, founded in 2015 and part of the Y Combinator Summer 2015 batch. Based in San Francisco, it runs cohort-based fellowship programs grounded in experiential, feedback-rich learning: the Founder Fellows Program (10 months, Series A to pre-IPO), the Grove Fellows Program (6 months, pre-seed and seed founders), the Executive Fellows Program (6 months, senior leaders), plus corporate workshops and retreats. Its primary teaching methodology is T-groups — small-group experiential learning built on shared observation, collective accountability and repeated practice — a model brought from the Stanford Graduate School of Business by co-founder Dr. Carole Robin. Leaders In Tech reports more than 350 alumni founders running companies valued at over $75B. It is a leadership-development organization, not a software or API provider: it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable interface.

providers.name: Quipper
providers.description: Quipper is an online learning platform founded in 2010 that describes itself as a "Distributor of Wisdom," building web and mobile e-learning products that let students and teachers study and manage coursework regardless of geographic or economic circumstances. The company operates regional education services across Japan, Indonesia, and the Philippines, pairing digital lesson content and assessments with tools for schools and teachers. Quipper is a 500 Global portfolio company. As of this enrichment pass no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface was found on its public web properties; this profile captures its verified web and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Upcode Academy
providers.description: UpCode Academy was a Singapore-based coding school offering short bootcamps and part-time courses (SQL, Python, Web Development with Ruby on Rails, Data Science, Computer Vision, IoT) taught by industry practitioners. Operated by 40 Tasks, a 500 Global portfolio company whose earlier product was the LOCO location-based search app at 40tasks.com. The company appears defunct - upcodeacademy.com serves a Cloudflare 522 dead-origin error (a bare default server page by December 2025) and 40tasks.com no longer resolves in DNS (domain-squatted since about 2023). No public API surface was found.

providers.name: WorkAmerica
providers.description: WorkAmerica was a skilled-labor hiring marketplace that connected job seekers, employers, and educators to close the skills gap - "connecting education to employment, exclusively for the skilled labor force" (archived homepage, 2017). A 500 Global portfolio company, it appears defunct - the workamerica.co domain expired (registrar suspension page captured December 2018) and now 301-redirects to an unrelated Indonesian website. No public API, developer portal, GitHub organization, or packages were found.

providers.name: Yacob
providers.description: Yacob was a Dubai-based Intelligent Nutrition platform and 500 Global portfolio company that combined cashless school-meal payments with nutrition monitoring. Pupils paid for school meals with a stored-value card while parents topped up accounts online, tracked transactions in real time, set spend and food limits, flagged allergies, and reviewed the nutritional value of their children's meals. The company appears dormant, with yacob.com no longer resolving as of 2026, and no public API surface was ever found.

providers.name: Center for Parent Information and Resources
providers.description: The Center for Parent Information and Resources (CPIR) is a federally funded central hub of information and products for the national network of Parent Training and Information Centers (PTIs) and Community Parent Resource Centers (CPRCs). CPIR supports families and youth, with a focus on children and youth with disabilities, delivering resources via the Parent Center Hub website, the Buzz from the Hub newsletter, and an events calendar. No public developer API has been identified; content and updates are delivered through website browsing, newsletter subscription, and an embedded Google Calendar.

providers.name: CourseGuide
providers.description: CourseGuide is a portfolio-lead company in the API Evangelist network, surfaced from the 500 Global portfolio and mapped to coursereport.com. Course Report is a consumer-facing education platform that helps prospective students discover, compare, and review coding bootcamps, certification courses, and professional training programs, aggregating 900+ programs and tens of thousands of alumni reviews alongside rankings, career-matching tools, and guidance content. No public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API surface was found during enrichment; this profile remains a lead with only domain-security posture and public web properties captured.

providers.name: Já Entendi
providers.description: Já Entendi is a Brazilian corporate-education (EdTech) company based in Curitiba that converts traditional corporate training materials into short, video-based online courses designed for workforces with lower levels of formal education. Its learning platform combines andragogy, heutagogy, storytelling, neurolinguistics, instructional design, and mind mapping to deliver more effective learning, offering both custom-built training solutions for large employee bases with sensitive or confidential content and a catalog of ready-made courses, all with integrated video lessons, assessments, and exercises. The company reports 1.2M+ students, 100+ courses, and 1,600+ videos delivered. Backed by 500 Global. No public developer portal, API, or SDK is published.

providers.name: Maqsad
providers.description: Maqsad is Pakistan's leading online entry-test preparation platform, helping students prepare for standardized university entrance exams including MDCAT, ECAT, BCAT and O-Level. The platform delivers daily live classes, recorded video lectures, 15,000+ practice MCQs per exam, weekly mock tests, real-time doubt-solving and academic counseling through student-facing mobile apps and web access. Founded in 2021 and backed by Speedinvest, Maqsad reports 4M+ downloads and tens of thousands of enrolled students placed into universities such as NUST, IBA and DUHS. It operates as a business-to-consumer education company and does not currently publish a developer API, documentation or developer portal.

providers.name: Wiley
providers.description: A global publishing and education company providing research, professional development, and learning solutions. Publishes peer-reviewed journals, textbooks, and digital content across science, technology, medicine, social science, and business.

providers.name: Job Corps
providers.description: Job Corps is the nation's largest free residential education and job training program for young adults, operated by the U.S. Department of Labor. It helps eligible young people ages 16 through 24 improve the quality of their lives through vocational and academic training across 100+ training areas, 10 in-demand industries, and 120+ campuses nationwide.

providers.name: Leif
providers.description: Leif (Leif Technologies, Inc.) was a New York City education-finance technology company, founded in 2017 by Francis Larson, Jeffrey Groeber and Richard Lee, that built an end-to-end platform for designing, originating, servicing and financing outcomes-aligned tuition products for schools and bootcamps. Its product line covered Income Share Agreements, contingent payment plans, tuition installment plans and upfront payment, alongside career-services and advisory-insights modules, and the platform handled student identity verification, credit evaluation, income verification, disbursement, payment collection and program reporting for its school partners. Leif publicly claimed more than 20,000 originations across 200+ partner schools and over $400 million in arranged financing, and it raised a strategic financing round totalling more than $60 million in 2021. Leif never operated a public developer program: the archived marketing site carries no developer portal, API reference or documentation nav, and the only API surface ever visible was the private JSON API behind its own student and school applications (leif.org/api/*). As of the 2026-08-25 probe the company's entire public surface is dark — leif.org and www.leif.org fail the TLS handshake at their Webflow edge, app.leif.org returns 504 on every path, the Zendesk help center is gone, and the api.leif.org and sandbox.leif.org AWS API Gateway hosts answer only "Missing Authentication Token".

providers.name: LessonLeap
providers.description: LessonLeap was a group-learning platform for children, offering small-group online classes and tutoring aimed at helping kids keep learning outside of school. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Point Nine and added to the API Evangelist network as an enrichment lead. LessonLeap has since been acquired by Preply, the language-learning and tutoring marketplace, and no longer operates as an independent product. lessonleap.com now serves only a single-page acquisition notice directing visitors to Preply. Enrichment probes on 2026-07-19 found no developer portal, no documentation, no API, no SDKs or packages, no public GitHub repositories, and no published .well-known discovery documents — this profile is retained as a historical company record rather than an API provider.

providers.name: LookSharp
providers.description: LookSharp (formerly InternMatch) was the largest internship and entry-level jobs marketplace dedicated entirely to US college students and new grads, connecting a marketplace of job-seeking students with employers who used its enterprise recruiting products to build employment brand and streamline campus hiring. Founded in 2009 by Andrew Maguire and Nathan Parcells and backed by 500 Global, LookSharp was acquired by WayUp in 2017; its internmatch.com domain now redirects to wayup.com and the brand no longer operates independently. This profile documents a defunct/acquired company with no public API or developer surface.

providers.name: OpenEnglish
providers.description: Open English is an online English-language learning company founded in 2007 and headquartered in Miami, serving primarily Latin American and Hispanic markets. It offers live, around-the-clock online classes with native-speaking teachers, self-paced interactive lessons, and mobile apps across consumer (B2C), business (Open English for Business), and children's (Open English Junior) programs. Backed by Insight Partners and other growth investors, it operates a consumer education platform and does not publish a public developer API program; its public GitHub organization holds internal open-source engineering forks rather than client SDKs.

providers.name: YellowBrink
providers.description: YellowBrink is a Netherlands-based, vendor-neutral community platform for open health data, founded by Jan de Lange and Bouwe Koopal to connect healthcare professionals, vendors, researchers and policymakers working with open standards such as openEHR, HL7 FHIR, OMOP and SNOMED CT. The name pairs the Yellow Pages — showing who builds what — with "brink", the Dutch word for the village square where a community gathers. It runs weekly webinars in cooperation with openEHR NL, country and topic special-interest groups, and discussion and co-creation rooms, hosts "The Brink" partner and meeting area at the EHRCON26 conference in Amsterdam, and is developing a postdoctoral European Master of Data Availability programme with European universities and hospital systems. The platform is a white-labelled Innoloft LoftOS tenant; YellowBrink itself publishes no public API, SDK or developer program.

providers.name: Kano Computing
providers.description: Kano Computing is a London-based technology company founded in 2013 by Alex Klein, Saul Klein and Yonatan Raz-Fridman that began by shipping build-it-yourself computer and coding kits designed to teach STEM and creative computing to children on top of Raspberry Pi hardware. Its catalog spanned the Kano Computer Kit, motion-sensor and Harry Potter / Star Wars coding wands, the Windows-based Kano PC built with Microsoft, and the Stem Player and Stem Video Projector consumer devices. Kano paired the hardware with Kano Code, a block-to-text creative-coding platform, and Kano World, an online making and sharing community. The company entered administration in 2023 and its assets now trade under the Stem brand; its developer footprint survives as open-source tooling in the KanoComputing GitHub organization and the npm @kano scope rather than a hosted API.

providers.name: 61draw
providers.description: 61draw (广东省六一线上非学科培训学校有限公司, Guangdong Liuyi Online Non-Academic Training School Co., Ltd.) is a China-based online children's art and non-academic education platform delivering live-broadcast art lessons to children roughly aged five to nine. It is a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and Matrix Partners China, which co-led its Series B round, and was surfaced to the API Evangelist network as a venture-portfolio lead. The company runs a consumer web and mobile presence at 61draw.com; no public developer, API, or documentation surface has been found during enrichment.

providers.name: Achieve3000
providers.description: Achieve3000 is a supplemental digital literacy solution for grades 3-12 that uses adaptive technology to personalize reading instruction, delivering differentiated nonfiction texts matched to each student's Lexile reading level to build vocabulary and comprehension. Originally an independent education-technology company backed by Insight Partners, Achieve3000 was acquired by McGraw Hill and is now offered as "Achieve3000 Literacy" within McGraw Hill's PreK-12 portfolio. Students and educators access the platform through their district's approved single sign-on (SSO); the product publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or SDKs. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network for discovery and demand tracking.

providers.name: Blinkist
providers.description: Blinkist is a Berlin-founded subscription learning app that condenses the key ideas of thousands of nonfiction books and podcasts into roughly 15-minute text and audio summaries called "Blinks." Launched in 2012, it is used by millions of readers to learn on the go across categories such as productivity, business, psychology, personal growth, and science, and it also offers Blinkist for Business for teams and organizations. The consumer product is delivered through the web and iOS/Android apps backed by a private mobile backend at api.blinkist.com; Blinkist does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or a developer portal. Blinkist was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company lead (backed by Insight Partners) and enriched with the provider signals that could be verified from its public surface.

providers.name: Blue Studios
providers.description: Blue Studios Labs is a family-focused technology company operating under the tagline "Where Families Flourish." It builds consumer digital products that help couples and families explore, learn, and grow together. Its portfolio includes Wallio, a shared financial-management app for couples and families; Blue Studios EDU, an entertainment-based educational streaming service; and Blue Studios Entertainment, a media-production studio creating family-oriented narratives and content. The company reports more than 400 million digital views, 350,000 game plays, and 4,000+ classes delivered. Blue Studios is a Techstars portfolio company. As of this profile it publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: Blue Studios.io, BlueStudios
providers.description: Blue Studios (bluestudios.io), tagline "Where Families Flourish," is a family-focused technology company backed by 500 Global that builds consumer digital products and experiences for households. Its portfolio spans Wallio, a collaborative finance app for couples and families; Blue Studios Education, an edutainment streaming and learning platform; Blue Studios Entertainment, a family-oriented media production division; and Blueniverse, the ecosystem tying the products together. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or developer documentation — this profile is a consumer-company record in the API Evangelist network rather than an API producer.

providers.name: BrightBytes
providers.description: BrightBytes was a San Francisco-based K-12 education data and analytics company founded in 2012 by Rob Mancabelli, best known for Clarity, a decision-support and analytics platform used by schools and districts to connect technology spending and classroom use to student learning outcomes, and for DataSense, a data-integration platform that captured, cleaned, and synced student data between disparate school systems. The company sold DataSense and its team to Microsoft in February 2019 and was itself acquired by Google in 2022. BrightBytes no longer operates independently: as of July 2026 www.brightbytes.net returns an expired-site placeholder and no developer portal, documentation, API, SDK, or status surface remains. This profile is retained as a historical company record with no API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Buildspace
providers.description: Buildspace was an online education platform and community that billed itself as "the biggest school in the world for people who wanted to work on their own ideas," running six-week cohort-based programs to help entrepreneurs and builders ship their own projects and startups. Backed by a16z, the company wound down its operations; its site now serves only a farewell letter and final video. It was a consumer education and community product, not an API provider, and exposes no public developer surface, API, documentation, or SDKs. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead.

providers.name: Byjus
providers.description: Byju's is an Indian educational technology company founded in 2011 by Byju Raveendran and Divya Gokulnath and headquartered in Bengaluru, India. It offered app-based adaptive learning for K-12 students and preparation for competitive exams such as JEE, NEET, and civil services, and expanded through acquisitions including Aakash, WhiteHat Jr, Toppr, Osmo, Epic, and Great Learning. Once among the world's most valuable edtech startups, the company entered insolvency proceedings in India following a widely reported financial collapse. Byju's does not publish a public developer program or API; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record awaiting any future developer surface.

providers.name: Chalkable
providers.description: Chalkable was a K-12 education technology company that provided a cloud-based student information system (SIS), learning management, and an education "app store" letting schools run third-party classroom apps on top of shared student data. Its developer platform exposed a RESTful API (OAuth 2.0) over school data points such as student and teacher scheduling, real-time attendance, grading and discipline records, announcements, messaging, and notifications, with partner apps rendered inside an iframe within the Chalkable classroom. Chalkable was acquired by PowerSchool on October 12, 2016, and the product line was absorbed into PowerSchool; the original developer surface (dev.chalkable.com and classroom.chalkable.com/Developer) is no longer operational. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment.

providers.name: Clutch Learning
providers.description: Clutch Learning (Clutch Prep) was a Miami-based education-technology startup founded in 2011 that helped more than two million college students learn through thousands of short-form, topic-based video tutorials and practice problems across subjects such as chemistry, physics, biology, accounting, and calculus. Backed by 500 Global (500 Startups), the company was acquired by Pearson in 2022 and folded into the Pearson+ study platform, where the offering now lives as Pearson Channels. The standalone clutchprep.com product is no longer independently operated. The domain 301-redirects to pearson.com/channels, and the company exposes no independent developer portal, public API, SDKs, or event surface. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as an acquired-company record.

providers.name: docin
providers.description: docin (豆丁网, docin.com) is a Chinese C2C document-sharing platform operated by Beijing Docin Century Network Technology (北京豆丁世纪网络技术有限公司) that faces the global market. The platform hosts over 1.3 billion documents, books, magazines, and publications spanning education, architecture and construction, business and contracts, medical and psychological materials, industry reports, and legal documents, supporting both learning and practical application. It offers a "豆丁书房" (Docin Reading Room) mobile reading app and VIP membership tiers. docin was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. Probing found no public developer or API platform: open.docin.com 301-redirects to the homepage, /app/api returns 404, and no /.well-known discovery documents are published.

providers.name: Edia
providers.description: Edia is an AI platform for K-12 school districts focused on improving student outcomes. Its products span AI math tutoring (reported 8-23% score improvements), attendance intervention to reduce chronic absenteeism (up to 30% reduction), and District Intelligence analytics that consolidate data from student information systems (SIS), learning management systems (LMS), behavior, and wellness sources into a single view for educators and administrators. Edia reports serving 200+ districts and 500K+ students. The company is backed by Felicis and was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-sourced company profile. Edia does not currently publish a public developer portal, API reference, or API specification, so this profile carries only verifiable company identity and probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: Edmodo
providers.description: Edmodo was an education technology company that operated a K-12 social learning network and learning management platform connecting teachers, students, and parents, and at its peak ran a developer platform and app store for third-party education apps. It was acquired by NetDragon in 2018 and the service was shut down in September 2022. Surfaced as a portfolio company of union-square-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the edmodo.com domain resolves only to a parked lander page and exposes no live developer, API, or documentation surface.

providers.name: EduPristine
providers.description: EduPristine is a Mumbai-based finance, accounting, and analytics training institute founded in 2008, offering classroom and online certification-prep and professional up-skilling programs. Its catalog spans financial modeling, CFA, FRM, ACCA, US CPA and US CMA, business analytics and data science, digital marketing, financial accounting (Big 4 aligned), and healthcare/medical coding. EduPristine runs training centers across India alongside self-paced and instructor-led online courses, and is part of Adtalem Global Education. Sector: edtech. No public developer API or documented API surface was found during enrichment; the corporate website sits behind a WAF that blocks automated discovery of a well-known or developer surface.

providers.name: English Central
providers.description: English Central is an online English language learning platform that combines a large library of authentic video content with speech-recognition-driven pronunciation practice, adaptive vocabulary and quiz tools, and live one-on-one lessons with tutors. It serves individual learners as well as schools, universities, and enterprise/partner programs (including regional partners in Japan and elsewhere). Backed by GV (Google Ventures), it operates in the consumer education / EdTech sector. No public developer API, SDK, or developer portal was found during enrichment; partner integrations appear to be handled privately.

providers.name: Izif
providers.description: Izif (إعزف) is an online music education platform for the Arabic-speaking world, positioning itself as the largest platform for teaching music in Arabic. It offers a subscription library of more than 2,000 instructional videos across roughly ten popular Arabic instruments — oud, guitar, violin, piano, ney, darbuka, qanun, vocals, and music theory — taught by elite Arab musicians, alongside music sheets and iOS/Android apps. A 500 Global portfolio company, Izif is a consumer EdTech subscription service and publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDK at this time.

providers.name: Kings
providers.description: Kings International Olympiads (kings.lt) is an international educational olympiads organization that runs academic competitions for students, operating a multi-language web platform served from kingsolympiad.com. It was surfaced through the 500 Global venture portfolio and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the organization publishes no public API, developer portal, documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable discovery artifacts (/.well-known/*, llms.txt all resolve to the SPA shell, i.e. soft 404s).

providers.name: liangzizhige
providers.description: liangzizhige.com is the corporate domain of QuantaSing Group Limited (NASDAQ QSG), a China-based online learning company listed by Qiming Venture Partners in its technology portfolio as a provider of personal finance online courses. As of this enrichment pass the liangzizhige.com domain is registered through Alibaba Cloud but publishes no A record and serves no website; the only live company surface found is the investor-relations site, which redirects to ir.quantasing.com. No developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI specification, public GitHub organization, or published client libraries were found for this company.

providers.name: Likeplum
providers.description: Likeplum (likeplum.com) was an online expert-knowledge and task marketplace that billed itself as "expert knowledge and skills at your fingertips" and invited users to "ask experts to answer your questions and hire skilled engineers, programmers, designers, writers, marketers and more on the world's largest information trading marketplace." Members posted either a free-to-ask question or a paid task, received answers and completed work from the site's expert pool, and paid only after approving the result under a post-pay model, with optional fully private posts and card or PayPal settlement. Its busiest categories were writing, programming, graphic design, and marketing and SEO. By late 2014 the company had folded the brand into the "Createpool" network, splitting its four most popular categories into dedicated sites — hackerpool.com for programming tasks, studypool.com for academic and homework Q&A, mechanicpool.com for auto repair, and counselpool.com for legal questions — and migrated every likeplum account, question, answer, and profile across. Only the academic property survives today: likeplum.com now 301-redirects to www.studypool.com, while createpool.com fails TLS negotiation and hackerpool.com, mechanicpool.com, and counselpool.com no longer resolve. The Likeplum brand exposes no developer portal, documentation, SDK, package, or public API, so this profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as an identity record for a rebranded 500 Global portfolio company rather than as an API provider.

providers.name: Lynda.com
providers.description: Lynda.com was an online video learning platform founded in 1995 by Lynda Weinman and Bruce Heavin, offering courses in software, creative, and business skills. LinkedIn acquired Lynda.com in 2015 (~$1.5B) and folded it into LinkedIn Learning; the standalone Lynda.com service has been retired and www.lynda.com now 301-redirects to linkedin.com/learning. The brand exposes no public developer program or API surface of its own. This profile was surfaced as an Accel portfolio company and enriched as a lead; the honest result is a defunct brand with no first-party API.

providers.name: Mujer Financiera
providers.description: Mujer Financiera is a Latin American financial-education platform founded in 2018 in Buenos Aires, Argentina by Sabrina Castelli, focused on closing the gender gap in financial inclusion. It delivers courses, packs, and multi-month programs (MF Platinum) on budgeting, saving, and investing, alongside a mobile app for tracking personal finances, a supportive community, a newsletter, and corporate financial-education services for companies. The platform reports hundreds of thousands of women served across 12+ countries and is backed by 500 Global. It is a business-to-consumer fintech/edtech offering and publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs; this profile captures its public identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Outsmart
providers.description: Outsmart (Outsmart Education) is an early-stage EdTech startup building a consumer, mobile-first learning experience for higher education in the age of AI — "the university of the future." Founded by former Duolingo executives and backed by roughly $38M from investors including Forerunner, Khosla, Lightspeed, DST, Abstract, Karman, Latitud, and Reach, with teams in LA, SF, and Salt Lake City. The product is a pre-launch waitlist app (iOS and Android, built with React Native, Rive, and Unity) emphasizing content generation at scale, gamification, and benchmarking. As of this profile the company publishes a marketing/waitlist site only; it exposes no public API, developer portal, or documentation.

providers.name: Playcurio
providers.description: PlayCurio is a Seoul-based educational technology company that builds AR (augmented reality) play-learning products for children, pairing physical educational tools with digital content. Its catalog includes AR titles such as Curio Safari, Phonics Pop, Dictionary Pop, and Math Mates, alongside a content-IP business spanning characters like Detective Pete, Dino Tales, and 100+ Curio Safari animals, plus B2B production services (character development, 2D/3D animation, UI/UX, and live-action video). PlayCurio is consumer- and partnership-facing and publishes no developer API, developer portal, SDKs, or API documentation. Surfaced via the 500 Global portfolio and enriched here; a domain-security probe of play-curio.com is the only technical artifact this pass produced.

providers.name: QLC
providers.description: QLC is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Its listed website resolves to NewCampus (newcampus.com), an education and financial operator that supports organizations across the innovation lifecycle — from early-stage incubation and acceleration through grants and treasury operations to leadership training, governance design, and operating-model consulting. Notable programs include the Open Campus Accelerator (OC-X) and the seachange HR and Web3 tracks. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, MCP server, or machine-readable specification — there is no developer surface to catalog beyond the corporate marketing site.

providers.name: ResearchGate
providers.description: ResearchGate is a professional network and social platform for scientists and researchers, founded in 2008 in Berlin, Germany. Members use it to share and discover research publications, connect and collaborate with colleagues, ask and answer questions, and track the reach and citations of their work. The platform hosts tens of millions of researcher profiles and a large corpus of full-text papers, and is operated by ResearchGate GmbH. It exposes no publicly documented developer API surface; this profile was surfaced via the dragoneer portfolio and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Salduu (Profe Social)
providers.description: Salduu, operating as Profe Social at profe.social, is a 500 Global-backed social networking platform. The live host serves Mastodon's default robots.txt (Disallow /search, sitemap.xml.gz) and a Ruby on Rails error stack, indicating the platform runs on Mastodon / ActivityPub fediverse technology, so it exposes the standard Mastodon client REST API and ActivityPub federation endpoints under /api. Both the site and its API surface sit behind a Cloudflare managed challenge, so the instance's own instance metadata, OpenAPI, and developer pages could not be retrieved by a non-browser client during enrichment. This profile records what was directly observed via DNS/TLS/HTTP and well-known probes; the API contract itself remains to be captured once the challenge is cleared or the provider publishes a spec.

providers.name: Socra AI
providers.description: Socra AI operates Socra Tutor (소크라 튜터), a Korean-market, AI-powered education service that describes itself as an intelligent AI answer-comparison service — students submit problems and Socra compares and evaluates candidate answers using AI to help them learn. It is a consumer-facing edtech mobile/web application rather than a developer platform; as of this profile no public API, developer portal, or technical documentation could be found. Socra AI was surfaced as a portfolio company of SoftBank Vision Fund and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment tracking.

providers.name: Socratic
providers.description: Socratic is an AI-powered homework help and learning app that lets students photograph or type a question and receive curated explanations, videos, and step-by-step resources across math, science, literature, and social studies. Founded in 2013 and backed at the early stage by investors including Andreessen Horowitz, Socratic was acquired by Google in 2018 and now operates as "Socratic by Google," a free consumer mobile app whose homework-help capabilities have largely been folded into Google Lens. Socratic publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or documented developer surface; this profile records it as an acquired consumer product with no independent API footprint.

providers.name: Sora
providers.description: Sora Schools is a fully online, project-based independent middle and high school (soraschools.com), backed by Union Square Ventures. Students learn through interdisciplinary, interest-driven projects and live small-group expeditions rather than traditional grade-level classes, with an accredited diploma path.
