It is surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a Union Square Ventures portfolio company. As of this enrichment pass the public site is served behind a Cloudflare bot challenge and Sora publishes no public developer, API, or integrations program, so this profile carries only probed infrastructure signals (DNS/TLS/security) rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: StudentFinance
providers.description: StudentFinance is a European fintech company, backed by Seedcamp, focused on financing access to education and career development (income-share and deferred-payment models for students and upskilling programs). Surfaced as a Seedcamp portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network, its public presence is currently a minimal Webflow marketing site; an enrichment pass found no public API, developer portal, documentation, SDKs, or /.well-known discovery surface.

providers.name: StudySoup
providers.description: StudySoup is a consumer education-technology platform that provides college and university students with study tools for better grades. It offers custom study guides written by student notetakers, step-by-step textbook solutions (AnswerED videos), video overviews of core curriculum (PreparED), and community features including a Discord channel and YouTube livestreams, alongside a notetaker monetization program that pays students to share their notes. StudySoup was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead. As of this enrichment pass the live site (studysoup.com) is an active B2C study-resources product with no publicly documented API, developer portal, SDKs, or integration surface.

providers.name: TeachStreet
providers.description: TeachStreet was an online learning marketplace that, in its own words, "helps people find great classes, courses, teachers, and instructors who help them learn new things," while "teachers use TeachStreet to find more students" (teachstreet.com homepage, archived June 2011). Surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a 500 Global portfolio company, TeachStreet was acquired by Amazon on February 2, 2012 and subsequently wound down. The teachstreet.com domain is now a dormant, Amazon-controlled brand-protection asset — MarkMonitor nameservers, a locked-down mail posture (SPF "v=spf1 -all", DMARC "p=reject" reporting to dmarc.amazon.com), and no A/AAAA/MX records — so there is no live website, developer portal, or API surface to enrich. This record is retained as a historical, defunct-company profile.

providers.name: VIPThink
providers.description: VIPThink (豌豆思维) is a Chinese online education company operated by Guangdong Happy Seeds Technology Co., Ltd. (广东快乐种子科技有限公司), delivering small-class live-streaming courses in mathematical thinking and logic for young children (roughly ages 3-8). It is part of a family of consumer education brands that also includes Hualala drawing classes (画啦啦), Wandou speech training (豌豆口才), Gubi early-learning (咕比启蒙), and Little Lighthouse (小灯塔). The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of SoftBank Vision Fund and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass, VIPThink operates only consumer-facing web and mobile learning products and publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: Zuoyebang
providers.description: Zuoyebang (作业帮) is a Chinese educational technology company founded in 2015 and headquartered in Beijing, backed by SoftBank Vision Fund. It operates a "technology + education" online learning platform whose flagship homework-help app lets K-12 students photograph a problem to get step-by-step answers, on-demand tutoring, and self-study tools across all subjects, alongside math tutoring products aimed at elementary-school parents and teachers. It is a consumer mobile/web product with no public developer program, open platform, or documented API surface at the time of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Harris Computer
providers.description: Harris Computer is a constellation of companies acquiring and operating vertical market software businesses across the public sector, healthcare, utilities, financial services, education, and insurance markets. Harris Computer itself does not publish a unified public developer portal; APIs and integrations are delivered through its individual portfolio companies (such as Harris Local Government, Harris Utilities, Harris Healthcare, and Harris School Solutions). Harris Computer is a subsidiary of Constellation Software Inc.

providers.name: Ornikar
providers.description: Ornikar is a French online driving school and insurance company that guides consumers from earning their driving permit through to car, home, and pet insurance. Founded in France, it offers highway-code (code de la route) training, driving lessons, accelerated permit programs, point-recovery courses, and corporate road-safety training, alongside auto, home, and pet insurance products and CPF financing. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Partech and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: Consumer. No public developer API surface was found during the enrichment pass; only domain-security signals were probed.

providers.name: Hinsta
providers.description: Hintsa Performance is a Finnish performance-coaching company founded by Dr. Aki Hintsa, applying methods developed over 30+ years working with Formula 1 drivers and elite athletes to help executives, leaders, and individuals achieve sustainable success. Its "Circle of Better Life" model combines Nordic wellbeing with performance principles proven in Formula 1, delivered as bespoke coaching programs across three segments (sports, businesses, and individuals). The company reports 3,500+ intensive executive coaching programmes delivered for 500+ organisations. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global. No public API, developer portal, documentation, or discovery surface (.well-known, llms.txt) was found during enrichment — this is a non-API wellbeing/coaching business.

providers.name: MycroFriends
providers.description: MycroFriends is a consumer health and wellness company that helps people become healthier through education and coaching centered on the connection between the human microbiome, nutrition, and overall health. Founded by George Cigale (previously founder of the online tutoring company Tutor.com) and headquartered in New York City, the company launched via a 2017 crowdfunding campaign and works with scientists, physicians, dietitians, and technologists to deliver microbiome education, personalized nutritional and lifestyle guidance, and access to expert health coaches. It was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Bloomberg Beta. As of this enrichment pass MycroFriends publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable API surface, and its former website resolves only to a default (unconfigured) Azure App Service host.

providers.name: Opencurriculum
providers.description: OpenCurriculum is a nonprofit education-technology organization (a Y Combinator alum) that builds curriculum-planning software for K-12 schools. Its web application helps teachers and administrators create and organize lesson plans, unit plans, and courses; draw on a curated library of high-quality, ready-to-go teaching ideas, resources, and strategies; align instruction to standards and learning goals; collaborate with colleagues on instructional design; and track progress through planner, calendar, and semester views with alignment analytics. The organization is based in Sacramento, California. As of this enrichment pass OpenCurriculum publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, OpenAPI specification, webhooks, or /.well-known discovery surface; it maintains a small public GitHub organization (one public repository, "flow", an open-source learning-app maker). This profile therefore carries company identity only, with no API artifacts to enrich.

providers.name: Talk Labs
providers.description: Talk Labs (TalkLabs) builds AI-powered voice simulations for corporate learning, turning training theory into practical, hands-on skills. Its platform provides AI trainers that role-play realistic customer scenarios so frontline sales and customer-service staff can practice conversations on demand. Capabilities include 24/7 AI coaching with no capacity limits, voice-based simulations in 50+ languages, progress-tracking and analytics dashboards, LMS integration, and a no-code AI lesson builder, with deployment within a week of contract. It serves banks, retail, hospitality, financial services, and restaurants. Backed by 500 Global and founded by Serge Sarkisian (CEO) and Ilia Krotov (CTO). No public API, developer portal, documentation, or well-known discovery surface was found at the time of this profile.

providers.name: Smalt
providers.description: Smalt is a Berlin-based training academy and technology platform for the green-energy installation trades. It combines a B2B installation services business (solar and, increasingly, heat pumps and other climate-trade work) with an education platform that upskills and certifies installers, plus a franchise model that lets trained installers run their own training businesses on Smalt's learning materials and tooling. Founded in 2023 and backed by General Catalyst, noa, Owl Ventures, Heartfelt, La Famiglia and Loric Ventures, Smalt is a workforce/services company rather than an API provider; as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public API, developer portal, OpenAPI, or SDK surface to catalog.

providers.name: Traderion
providers.description: Traderion is a fintech company that combines technology and gamification to build digital learning platforms for banks and financial institutions. Its products include a gamified sales and trading simulator covering equities, FX, bonds, and commodities with AI-powered feedback, a MiFID II regulatory-compliance training platform built as a virtual simulated bank, and a risk-profiling platform for identifying and detecting risky behavioral patterns within organizations. A Seedcamp portfolio company, Traderion does not currently publish a public developer portal or API.

providers.name: Subtext *
providers.description: Subtext was a consumer/education social-reading and in-text annotation app backed by GV (listed in GV's portfolio with an asterisk denoting an exited investment). It has since been acquired: as of this enrichment pass the company domain subtext.com 301-redirects to renaissance.com (Renaissance Learning), and no independent website, developer portal, API, documentation, or /.well-known/security.txt could be found. No public API surface exists to enrich; this profile records the verified exit/redirect status and a domain-security probe of subtext.com.

providers.name: Frontrow
providers.description: FrontRow was an India-based edtech company that operated an online learning platform teaching extracurricular skills and hobbies — such as music, singing, guitar, drawing, chess and other creative pursuits — to learners through recorded video courses and community-driven classes. The company was backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners. As of the last enrichment pass the product has shut down: its primary domain frontrow.co.in 301-redirects to a Medium shutdown announcement confirming "FrontRow shut down a few months ago," and no developer portal, public API, documentation, or SDK surface exists. This entry is retained as a defunct portfolio-lead record; there are no live API artifacts to enrich.

providers.name: MommaZoo
providers.description: MommaZoo was a mobile web application for parent-teacher and school-community communication, surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Built as an HTML5 cross-platform app, it let parents and teachers centralize class posts, homework, sign-ups, reminders, documents, and multi-channel messaging across devices and languages. The company is defunct - public activity ends around 2013 and the mommazoo.com domain is now parked - and an enrichment pass found no developer portal, documentation, or public API surface.

providers.name: Orbis Education
providers.description: Orbis Education is a healthcare education services company founded in 2003 that partners with universities and healthcare systems to create, market, and manage collaborative, accelerated healthcare degree programs — including Accelerated Bachelor of Science in Nursing (ABSN), Medical Laboratory Sciences (MLS), and Occupational Therapy Assistant (OTA) programs — to help address workforce shortages in nursing and allied health. Operating across more than 26 states, the company connects students with universities and clinical placement sites to graduate practice-ready professionals, and was acquired by Grand Canyon Education in 2018. Orbis Education is a services provider and does not publish a public API, developer portal, or developer documentation.

providers.name: Pathgather
providers.description: Pathgather was an enterprise Learning Experience Platform (LXP), founded in 2012 and headquartered in New York City, that helped large enterprises curate, share, and track learning content across their existing learning ecosystems. Backed by Bloomberg Beta and Techstars, Pathgather (co-founded by CEO Eric Duffy) was one of the companies that established the LXP category before being acquired by Degreed in June 2018; all employees joined Degreed and the standalone product was wound down. Pathgather exposed a REST API in its operating years (a community Python client, tonybaloney/pathgather, remains on PyPI as historical evidence), but the company no longer operates independently: the pathgather.com domain is now parked and publishes no live API, developer portal, or documentation surface. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as an acquired/defunct company record.

providers.name: OnlineTyari
providers.description: OnlineTyari is one of India's largest online exam-preparation platforms, built by Next Door Learning Solutions Private Limited (Jaipur, Rajasthan) and acquired by Embibe in February 2020. Through its website and Android/iOS apps it helps students and job aspirants prepare for competitive government examinations such as SSC CGL, IBPS PO/Clerk, RRB, Railways NTPC, and various State PSC exams, offering mock tests, question banks, current-affairs updates, e-books, and study material in Hindi and English produced with independent tutors, coaching institutes, and subject authors. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass, OnlineTyari operates as a consumer-facing exam-prep product and publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal.

providers.name: Almentor
providers.description: Almentor is a Dubai (UAE) based video e-learning platform delivering the largest high-quality Arabic continuous-learning video library, founded in 2016 and launched in January 2018 by Ihab Fikry and Ibrahim Kamel. It serves both individual learners (B2C) and organizations (B2B via business.almentor.net) with paid courses, free talks, crash courses, and books across health, humanities, technology, entrepreneurship, business management, lifestyle, and corporate communication, delivered by hundreds of experts and educators across the MENA region. Backed by Partech, Almentor has delivered more than three million learning experiences. Almentor publishes no public developer/API program; this profile is maintained as a company record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: AltSchool
providers.description: AltSchool was an American education-technology company founded in 2013 by former Google executive Max Ventilla to build a network of small private "lab" schools around a personalized, student-directed learning model, using those campuses to develop a K-12 software platform for assignments and progress tracking. It raised more than $170 million from investors including Founders Fund, Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Mark Zuckerberg's CZI, and Peter Thiel. In 2017-2019 the company closed or handed off its for-profit schools (to Higher Ground Education) and pivoted to selling the software as "Altitude Learning," with Ventilla stepping down as CEO. The venture is now defunct as an independent operation: the altschool.com domain no longer resolves and altitudelearning.com redirects to Guidepost Montessori. No public developer, API, or documentation surface was found; this record is retained as a historical VC-portfolio company profile.

providers.name: Bluelearn
providers.description: Bluelearn was an India-based community-driven learning and edtech startup backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners, added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub for enrichment. As of this enrichment pass the company appears inactive - its primary domain (bluelearn.in) no longer serves a product site and instead resolves to a parked GoDaddy lander page, with no reachable HTTPS endpoint, developer portal, documentation, or public API surface. No OpenAPI, SDK, or other machine-readable API artifacts were found to search, generate, or derive from. This profile remains a lead pending any revived public developer surface.

providers.name: Briko Robotics
providers.description: Briko Robotics (Briko Robotica) was a Mexican educational technology startup founded in 2014 in San Luis Potosi, Mexico, that sold a modular programmable electronics kit paired with an online learning platform teaching robotics and programming to children from roughly age eight. The company was accelerated by 500 Startups LatAm (batch 7) and raised a small seed amount. Third-party company databases now classify Briko Robotics as deadpooled, and its former domain brikorobotics.com has been hijacked and serves unrelated SEO spam. No developer portal, documentation, API, or machine-readable specification was ever published, so this profile carries identity and provenance only.

providers.name: changeducation
providers.description: ChangEducation is an integrated teaching-service provider of artificial-intelligence and STEAM curriculum systems, surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. It builds AI and STEAM (Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts, Mathematics) curriculum products and teaching services for the Chinese K-12 education market. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes only a marketing website (changeducation.cn, which redirects to a JavaScript-rendered landing page) with no public developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI, SDKs, or documentation surface, so this profile remains an identity-only lead with no technical API artifacts.

providers.name: eduFire
providers.description: eduFire was an online education startup surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. An enrichment pass on 2026-07-19 found that the company's primary domain, edufire.com, no longer resolves (no DNS A or NS records), indicating the company is defunct. No live developer portal, API surface, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or any other artifact could be located to enrich, so this profile remains an identity-only stub.

providers.name: Edukart
providers.description: EduKart was an Indian online education startup, backed by 500 Startups (500 Global), that sold certificate, diploma and degree courses from partner universities and training institutes to Indian learners. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500-global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. The company is now defunct — repeated probes of edukart.com find a parked hosting placeholder rather than a live business, and no developer, API, documentation or SDK surface exists to catalog.

providers.name: Enuma, Inc.
providers.description: Enuma, Inc. is a Berkeley, California educational technology company that builds award-winning, self-guided digital learning apps for young children, including the Todo Math series, Todo Classroom, and the Kitkit School / Enuma Global program. Founded by Sooinn Lee and Gunho Lee, Enuma designs research-based, game-like early literacy and numeracy experiences that work for all learners, including children with special needs and those in low-resource settings. The company co-won the $10M Global Learning XPRIZE for its open-source Kitkit School tablet curriculum. Enuma is a consumer and classroom education company that ships mobile applications through the Apple App Store and Google Play; it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or event surface. This profile was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and enriched with verified company identity by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Funderful
providers.description: Funderful was an alumni fundraising software platform for universities and higher-education advancement teams, founded in 2013 by Raimonds Kulbergs and headquartered in Riga, Latvia. It helped advancement offices run donation campaigns, track donors, and pioneer conversational chatbots to re-engage alumni, with clients including UC Berkeley, Georgetown, London Business School, and Oxford and Cambridge colleges. Funderful joined 500 Startups (Batch 20) and raised seed funding before being acquired by Ruffalo Noel Levitz (RNL) in February 2019. The company is defunct as an independent entity and its domain (funderful.com) no longer resolves; enrichment found no live developer portal, documentation, or public API surface.

providers.name: GamerzClass
providers.description: GamerzClass was a Copenhagen, Denmark-based online esports education platform, founded in 2018, that offered structured masterclasses and one-on-one coaching from professional players across titles such as Counter-Strike, League of Legends, and Dota 2. Backed by 500 Global, ByFounders, Bumble Ventures, and TrueSight Ventures, the company raised roughly USD 2.5M before being acquired by US-based esports coaching marketplace Metafy in May 2022. The gamerzclass.com domain no longer serves a live site and the company exposes no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface.

providers.name: InstaEDU
providers.description: InstaEDU was an online, on-demand tutoring platform founded in 2011 in San Francisco that connected students with tutors for live one-on-one help across a range of academic subjects. Backed by Battery Ventures and Social Capital, the company was acquired by Chegg in 2014 and folded into the Chegg Tutors service, which Chegg subsequently wound down in 2021. There is no independent InstaEDU developer program, public API, developer portal, or live domain today (instaedu.com no longer resolves) — this profile is retained as a historical portfolio lead in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Jumpcut
providers.description: Jumpcut (Jumpcut, Inc.) is a Y Combinator-backed, remote-first digital-media company founded in 2014 in Los Angeles that produces online courses about entrepreneurship and content creation — teaching viral YouTube growth, audience building, and launching digital products with marketing automation. It reached the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of 500 Global and Canaan Partners. Jumpcut is a consumer education/creator business, not an API producer: it publishes no developer platform, API reference, or machine-readable API specification, so there is no API surface to onboard here. As of this profile its primary domain jumpcut.com does not resolve (registered via Namecheap through 2032 but serving no DNS/website), and customers reported losing account access in late 2025, indicating the product has wound down. Retained as an identity-only network stub.

providers.name: juren
providers.description: Juren (巨人教育 / Juren Education) is a Chinese comprehensive basic-education training institution founded in 1994 and headquartered in Beijing (Zhongguancun, Haidian District). It is a B2C education and tutoring business — spanning brands such as Juren School, Juren 1-on-1, Xiao Juren, and Juren online school — offering courses in Chinese, English, mathematics, arts, study tours, and seasonal camps, plus education publishing and franchising. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of the venture firm Qiming and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. Enrichment found NO public developer, API, or technical-integration surface: the historic official domain juren.com does not resolve (DNS), juren.ai is a parked for-sale domain, and juren.cn is a Chinese-language marketing mirror with no developer section. This is a non-API B2C company lead retained for network completeness rather than API artifact enrichment.

providers.name: KNO
providers.description: Kno, Inc. was a digital textbook and student learning platform founded in May 2009 in Santa Clara, California by CEO Osman Rashid (co-founder of Chegg) and CTO Babur Habib. Kno began as a dual-screen tablet built for students, abandoned hardware in 2011, and pivoted to eTextbook software delivered across iPad, Android, Windows and the web in partnership with textbook publishers. The company raised roughly $93 million from Andreessen Horowitz, Intel Capital, Goldman Sachs, FLOODGATE, First Round Capital, SV Angel, Advance Publications and GSV Capital before being acquired by Intel in November 2013 for approximately $15 million and rebranded as Intel Education Study, which has itself since been discontinued. As of enrichment the kno.com domain is parked and redirects to a third-party domain brokerage, and the provider exposes no public API, developer portal, documentation, SDK, or other artifact surface to enrich.

providers.name: LearnSprout
providers.description: LearnSprout was a San Francisco edtech company founded in 2012 by Franklyn Chien, Anthony Wu and Joe Woo out of the Imagine K12 accelerator. It built LearnSprout Connect, an API layer that unlocked K-12 student data held in student information systems (SIS) through direct database integration rather than the SIS application layer, giving edtech developers a single "once and done" integration plus a change-log endpoint for incremental syncs. It also sold a district-facing analytics product covering attendance, grades and college readiness, reaching over 2,500 schools across 42 states on roughly $4.7M raised from Andreessen Horowitz, Formation 8 and Samsung Ventures. Apple acquired the company in January 2016 and the public API was retired; learnsprout.com no longer resolves and is parked on Apple nameservers.

providers.name: Make School
providers.description: Make School was a San Francisco-based computer science college and coding bootcamp, backed by a16z, that offered an applied computer science bachelor's program. As of August 2021 the degree program moved to Dominican University of California, and Make School.org now operates as a 501(c)(3) nonprofit running a scholarship program for former Bachelor in Applied Computer Science students. The organization publishes no public API, developer portal, or technical documentation. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub and this enrichment pass confirmed there is no API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Motion Math
providers.description: Motion Math was an educational math-games company (500 Global portfolio) whose products were acquired by Curriculum Associates and folded into the i-Ready learning platform. As of the enrichment probe (2026-07-20) the motionmathgames.com domain and every subdomain (developer/api/docs) return a 301 redirect to curriculumassociates.com/products/i-ready/i-ready-learning/motionmath-shutdown, and the site shares a wildcard TLS certificate with i-ready.com. The company publishes no independent API, developer portal, documentation, SDK, or /.well-known discovery surface — this profile is retained as a network record of a defunct/acquired provider with no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: OneRoom
providers.description: OneRoom was an online-learning startup founded in 2014 in San Francisco by Scott Forman and Jeff Kolesky and backed by Bloomberg Beta's 2013 fund with a roughly $750K seed round. It operated joinoneroom.com as a marketplace of live, video-based writing courses (fiction, non-fiction, playwriting, poetry, and prose) taught in intimate online classrooms featuring break-outs, head-to-head debates, content sharing, and co-annotation. The company appears defunct — co-founder Jeff Kolesky departed in 2016, and its domain now 302-redirects to a domain-sale listing (hugedomains.com). No product, developer portal, documentation, or public API surface remains. This profile records the honest identity so the API Evangelist network does not re-research a dead portfolio lead.

providers.name: Smarterer
providers.description: Smarterer was a Boston-based skills-assessment company that used crowdsourced, adaptive tests to rapidly quantify people's proficiency across 400+ technical, social, and business skills. Backed by Google Ventures (GV), it opened a REST API in March 2015 that let partners embed tests, pull score data, and build leaderboards and profiles on top of its assessment engine. Pluralsight acquired Smarterer for roughly $75M in November 2014, absorbed its test engine into the Pluralsight learning platform, and wound down the standalone product. The smarterer.com domain no longer serves a site (defensively held via MarkMonitor, no DNS A record) and there is no live API surface to enrich.

providers.name: TakeLessons
providers.description: TakeLessons was an online and in-person lessons marketplace founded in 2007 by Steven Cox and headquartered in San Diego, California. It connected students with independent instructors for music, languages, academic subjects, cooking, and professional training, handling scheduling, payments, and instructor discovery. Microsoft acquired TakeLessons in September 2021 to expand its edtech offerings, then wound the service down: the last day to book lessons was August 15, 2024 and the consumer site closed on November 15, 2024. The company is now defunct and publishes no live website, developer portal, or API surface; this record is retained as a portfolio-lineage stub for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: The OK Company
providers.description: The OK Company was a consumer technology startup, backed by Obvious Ventures, best known for OK Play - a mobile app for iOS and Android that turned screen time into a catalyst for real-world, parent-and-child play activities designed to build empathy, kindness, and creativity in young children. It was founded by CEO JJ Aguhob and President Chris Ovitz (previously co-founders of the mobile video app Viddy), with developmental psychologist Dr. Colleen Russo Johnson as Chief Scientist. As of this enrichment pass the company appears defunct - its domain theokcompany.com no longer resolves to a product site and instead redirects to a third-party domain-sale listing. The OK Company was a consumer mobile app business and never published a public developer API, SDK, or developer platform, so there is no API surface to enrich. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio-company lead.

providers.name: Tiny Comet
providers.description: Tiny Comet is an educational games studio building history-based simulation RPGs for school-aged children, founded by Emily Tierney and Anca Agapi. Its first title, Nation Survival, is an immersive educational role-playing game on the Roblox platform. The studio came out of the a16z SPEEDRUN accelerator and has raised additional venture capital from Andreessen Horowitz and Roble Ventures. Tiny Comet is a consumer gaming and edtech company with no public developer or API surface at this time; this profile captures its identity in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Tutornow
providers.description: Tutornow (tutornow.it) is an Italian online tutoring platform ("ripetizioni") that connects students from elementary school through university with qualified tutors across 150+ subjects, including math, physics, chemistry, and languages. It offers individual and group online lessons starting around €15/hour, homework help, exam and university preparation, academic-recovery programs, and specialized support for students with learning differences (DSA/BES), with 250,000+ lesson hours delivered and 20,000+ tutors across major Italian cities. Tutornow is a consumer (B2C) education service and publishes no public developer API, API documentation, or developer portal — this profile is maintained as a company record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Ubooly
providers.description: Ubooly was a children's smart-toy company that made "The Learning Toy that Listens" - a plush toy that turned a smartphone, iPod touch, or tablet into an interactive learning companion for kids aged 4-8, with hand-crafted play packs and voice interaction. A 500 Global portfolio company, Ubooly is now defunct; ubooly.com was last archived as a live storefront in late 2015 and today 301-redirects to an unrelated third-party site. No public API, developer portal, packages, or GitHub organization were found.

providers.name: UCode
providers.description: UCode was a STEM coding-education company ("Where Kids Learn to Code and Create") that taught kids and teens ages 6-19 software programming through classes, camps, and online instruction, creating apps, websites, and games. A seed-stage Bloomberg Beta portfolio company founded by Scott Mueller and Michael Yang, it is marked as exited in the Bloomberg Beta Manual. As of 2026-07-21 ucode.com is a parked domain listed for sale, and no API, developer, or platform surface exists to enrich.

providers.name: Practice
providers.description: Practice (practice.do) was a Montreal-based all-in-one coaching and consulting business platform that bundled scheduling, client portals, forms, contracts, invoicing, and payments into a single tool for independent coaches. The company shut down permanently on November 3, 2025 after a failed acquisition process; its domain no longer serves a product and it exposes no public developer portal, documentation, or API surface.
